v1Mechanisms.name: 10. Prefetched hint ladder anchored on the learner's line
v1Mechanisms.spec:
SPECULATIVE PREFETCH:
- In onTick, when signals.score >= .6 and the task has no valid prefetch, enqueue a HintLadderSchema job: medium effort, priority 2, key 'hint:<taskId>', drawn from the 4/hour hint reserve (mechanism 1).
- The key is the task only. Validity is decided by the staleness rules, never by a hash of the prompt: gatherCodeContext embeds <<CURSOR>> and 'N min ago' notes, so a prompt hash changes whenever the cursor moves or a minute passes.
- contentHash = sha1 of the task files' text (CRLF normalised) plus the sorted error set. It is computed separately from prompt rendering, and used only to avoid re-firing for an identical state.
STALE RULES. Any one makes the prefetch invalid; re-fire only if the score is still >= .6 and contentHash differs from the last fired one:
- the anchor's lineText is no longer found in the file
- 20 or more lines changed since the prefetch (Monitor edit counter)
- the error set changed
- the task changed
CAPS:
- one hint job in flight per task
- stop after 2 unused prefetches in a task
- none when proactiveHints is 'off'
- at most 4 speculative hints per hour (the reserve)
POST-PARSE VALIDATION (zod refine is not enforced by constrained decoding, so this is checked after parsing): rung 1 and rung 2 text must end with '?' and contain no code fence. A failing rung is dropped and served on demand instead.
SERVING:
- At score >= 1 in 'offer' mode, a 'hint-ready' action is shown.
- In 'auto' mode, or on Ctrl+Alt+H / deliberate.hint, hint() serves the next rung from the prefetch immediately.
- On a miss: HintLadderSchema at LOW effort (was medium), about 10-15 s.
- Rungs 4-5 use HintSchema at low effort.
- Solo tasks: rungs above 2 and Reveal are unavailable.
RUNG 0 FOR ERRORS (local, no model):
- When a project-code error persists (the same exception in 2 terminal runs, or for 1+ min in diagnostics), the first help is 'Which line does the trace point at, and what does <ExceptionName> mean?' on the traced line. Uses parseException on the terminal tail (mechanism 2).
- Got it there records nothing; Next goes to rung 1.
DISPLAY (in the editor through the LineAnnotationManager, mechanism 4; the sidebar card stays as a log):
- Short rung text (52 characters or fewer):
  - after-text 'Hint 1: <text>' on the anchored line, italic, editorCodeLens.foreground
  - whole-line background editor.wordHighlightBackground
  - overview ruler mark: editorInfo.foreground, Right lane
- Longer text: a comment thread on the anchored line instead of truncated after-text.
  - createCommentController('deliberate.hints', 'Deliberate hints'), then createCommentThread(uri, range, [comment]).
  - Thread: canReply = false, collapsibleState Expanded, label 'Hint 2'.
  - Comment: body is a MarkdownString with isTrusted = {enabledCommands: ['deliberate.hint', 'deliberate.gotIt', 'deliberate.teach']} and the links '[Next hint](command:deliberate.hint) · [Got it](command:deliberate.gotIt)'; author {name: 'Deliberate'}; mode Preview.
  - The thread opens only when a hint is served, so the inline zone it inserts is learner-initiated.
- The anchor is re-resolved by searching for lineText (nearest match to the original line). If it is not found, the hint stays a sidebar card only.
- If the file is visible, revealRange(InCenterIfOutsideViewport) without taking focus. The tempo bar shows 'hint ready · cli.py:14'.
- Annotation and thread are disposed when the anchored line text changes, on Got it, or when a spec turns green.
RUNG MAPPING:
- Rung 1: Socratic question.
- Rung 2: if a verified atom exists for the diagnosed concept: 'Hint 2: this is <pattern name>. 60 s drill: Alt+N', and the 'atom' action is queued. The thread also shows the rung-2 text.
- Rung 3: plain-language steps.
- Rung 4: the skeleton opens in the pad in 'skeleton' mode, with header 'Skeleton for the stuck piece - fill the ___ here, then write it in your own file'. The ___ blanks are SnippetString placeholders. Ctrl+Enter closes the pad. Never inserted into project files.
- Rung 5: the smallest piece, shown in the thread and in a sidebar card with 'retype it'. Paste and assisted detection (mechanism 3) apply.
- gotIt(): records rung evidence (mechanism 3 weights), clears annotations, calls markProgress, and resumes building with no explain-back question.
PRE-HINT STEP: when an own-code probe is ready (mechanism 12) and this stuck episode has had no hint yet, the first help offered after rung 0 is 'Before a hint: predict one call (15 s)'. Its result is passed into the hint prompt.
KNOWN-GAP SHORTCUT: if the next red spec's concept is a gate-deferred gap and its JIT offer was skipped, the stuck threshold for this task is multiplied by .6.

v1Mechanisms.name: 11. Red-green spec ladder: sandboxed behaviour specs with fading titles and just-in-time drills
v1Mechanisms.spec:
SCOPE:
- V1 covers Python, JavaScript and TypeScript tasks whose core logic is plain functions. It needs a detected runtime and consent 'all'.
- Anything else (UI, network, interactive, Go/Java/Rust in V1, other languages) falls back to Check my work through mechanism 9.
INTERFACE FIRST: each task's interface (file and 1-3 signatures) comes from PlanOutline or TaskBatch (mechanism 7), so it is known before the learner types. The specs part of TaskPrep (mechanism 8) must conform to it.
SPECS ARE DATA, NOT TEST CODE: each spec is {call expression with literal args, expected literal or expected error class}. Our bundled harness runs them; the model never writes test code.
CALL AND EXPECTED VALIDATION (before anything is stored, for visible and hidden specs alike):
- validateCall (pure TS, shared with mechanism 12) accepts exactly one call whose callee is a name in interface.functions and whose arguments are literals only:
  - Python keyword arguments name=literal are allowed
  - literals: numbers, strings, booleans, None/null/undefined, lists, tuples, dicts/objects of literals, unary minus
  - anything else is dropped
- expected is parsed only as a literal, never evaluated: the Python-literal parser or ast.literal_eval in the harness; JSON.parse in Node.
- Workspace content in the prompt therefore cannot inject code that runs on every save.
VERIFICATION AT PREFETCH TIME (learner-code sandbox, mechanism 2):
- Build a temp copy of the workspace's source files: language globs, excluding node_modules, .git, venv, .venv, dist, build and __pycache__; capped at 2 MB and 300 files. node_modules is linked in as a junction (win32) or symlink.
- Reference variant: every visible and hidden spec must pass.
  - If the interface file does not exist or defines none of the interface functions, write the reference as that file.
  - Otherwise replace each interface function's range (executeDocumentSymbolProvider on the learner's file, regex fallback) with the reference version, appending reference helpers.
- Stub variant: the learner's current file (or an empty one), with the interface functions replaced by stubs that raise NotImplementedError / throw. Every spec must fail cleanly: failed, not a harness crash.
- Delete the temp dirs at once.
- The reference is never stored in Project state, never logged, and never sent to another prompt or gatherCodeContext. This keeps 'never write their code' intact.
- On a verification failure: one low-effort repair call with the failing spec ids and actual values. Specs that still fail are dropped. Fewer than 3 left: applicable = false.
ATTACHING:
- At task start the card shows the interface ('Write in cli.py: parse_args(argv) -> dict'; JS adds 'export') whether or not specs have landed, plus the spec titles allowed by Task.fade.
- Specs that land while the task is building attach immediately. The tempo bar shows 'specs ready (5)' without a pop, and they run on the next save.
- If the learner's file already differs from the interface:
  - map each interface function to theirs by exact name, else by a unique function of the same arity in the interface file, and rewrite the spec calls to their names
  - if no mapping exists, mark the ladder not applicable, with the card 'Your design differs from the planned interface; Check my work will review it instead.'
  - never force a rename
- Done when all specs are green. acceptanceCriteria stay as the review fallback.
TRIGGERS:
- Manual save of any task file (TextDocumentSaveReason.Manual, from onWillSaveTextDocument): run at once (debounced 300 ms).
- Auto-save (AfterDelay or FocusOut): run only after 1.5 s without edits, and only when the file has no Error-severity diagnostics, so half-typed code does not flicker red.
- Learner-started runs from the Testing view, and continuous runs (request.continuous). When continuous mode is on, saves do not also trigger runs.
RUNS:
- Spec data JSON is written to globalStorageUri/specs/<taskId>.json, never into the workspace.
- runLearnerCode runs media/harness/harness.py or harness.mjs with the learner-code profile: cwd = a fresh temp dir, the workspace on the module path read-only, the audit hook (Python), permission flags (Node), stdin ignored, 5 s total timeout.
- The harness reports importMs. If the first run's import takes over 1 s (pandas, flask and similar), the timeout becomes 5 s + importMs and the tempo bar shows 'running specs...' during runs. A persistent per-task worker is in v2.
MODULE LOADING:
- Python:
  - The module is imported normally under a non-__main__ name ('dlb_<module>'). 'if __name__ == '__main__'' blocks do not run, while ordinary top-level assignments such as PATTERN = re.compile(...) or counts = Counter() do.
  - builtins.input is patched to raise DeliberateTopLevel. sys.argv is a sentinel list that raises it on any access beyond index 0. A top-level run longer than the timeout is reported the same way.
  - Any of these gives the teachable nudge 'top-level code runs on import: move it under if __name__ == '__main__''.
  - This replaces the earlier AST-strip loader, which deleted assignments with calls and contradicted the input() nudge.
- JS/TS:
  - Before importing, a top-level safety check. The file's top level may contain only imports, exports, declarations, function and class definitions, and const/let initialisers that call nothing except new Map/Set/RegExp/Array/Object, Object.freeze, Symbol, or arrow/function expressions.
  - If unsafe, the module is not imported, and the nudge is 'wrap the entry code in a main guard (if (require.main === module) or, on Node 24.2+, if (import.meta.main))'.
  - Then await import(pathToFileURL(file)), falling back to createRequire for CJS.
  - Interface names that are defined but not exported give the nudge 'parse_args is defined but not exported: add export'.
  - Promise results are awaited (2 s cap). Comparison: util.isDeepStrictEqual against JSON.parse(expected).
- TypeScript: Node type stripping with the resolve hook, or tsx (mechanism 2).
HARNESS PROTOCOL:
- Each spec prints '@@DLB_START <id>' before it runs and '@@DLB {json}' after, with {id, pass, actual (repr, 200 characters or fewer), error}.
- If a run times out, the spec that started last is reported as 'timeout (infinite loop?)' and the rest as not run.
REPORTING:
- Checked in the installed VS Code 1.140: testing.automaticallyOpenTestResults (formerly testing.openTesting) defaults to 'openOnTestStart', so a TestRun on every save would open Test Results over the learner's terminal. testing.automaticallyOpenPeekView defaults to 'never' there; its 1.93 default must be checked in a spike before the Testing view is relied on.
- Save-triggered runs never create a TestRun. Results go to a gutter icon per spec function (passed/failed), the LineAnnotationManager, the tempo bar ('3/5 · next: <title>') and the task card's ladder.
- Only the target spec (the first red one in ladder order) is reported as failed. Later red specs show as 'not yet', with no message or location, so the learner is never shown several failures on their def line at once.
- The TestController still lists the specs:
  - one root TestItem per task, one child per visible spec
  - uri and range = the function's def line, via executeDocumentSymbolProvider with a regex fallback
  - createRunProfile('Run specs', TestRunProfileKind.Run, handler, true, undefined, true)
- Its handler publishes TestRun results only for runs the learner starts, or continuous runs:
  - passed(item, ms)
  - failed for the target only, with TestMessage.diff(text, expected, actual) and location = the def line
  - skipped for later specs
  - errored with the stderr tail on a harness crash
- A failureSignature match on the target puts after-text on the learner's def line, e.g. 'spec 3: is -v a value or a flag?' (52 characters or fewer, full text in hover). Not shown in solo tasks.
FADING (Task.fade, mechanism 8):
- full: all titles.
- partial: the next title only; each later one is revealed as the previous turns green.
- minimal and solo: 'n of m behaviours pass', and for the failing target, the call and the learner's actual result (never the expected value).
JIT ATOM OFFERS:
- When the target spec changes and its conceptId has P < .5 or is a gate-deferred gap, the tempo text becomes 'next: <title> uses <pattern> · 60s drill? Alt+N' at that moment (no pop).
- It is offered once more on the first save that touches that spec's function.
- Not in solo tasks. Accepting opens the atom (mechanism 6).
EVIDENCE AND PROGRESS:
- The first time a spec turns green:
  - detector.markProgress(now, 'spec 3 green')
  - evidence kind 'spec' correct, production = true
  - full weight only within 3 saves since it went red and with the function not assisted; otherwise weight .3
  - latency = active ms since the previous green (or task start), against parSec
- Signature matches: passive misconception evidence (x1.5 odds, weight .5) and recordMistake(misconceptionId).
- A target spec still red past 2x par with the same signature twice queues an 'atom' offer for its concept.
ALL VISIBLE SPECS GREEN: run the hidden specs.
- Hidden pass: criteria met; flash; what-ifs (mechanism 12); completeTask. The polish review (WorkReviewSchema, medium, polish-only prompt) runs only when deliberate.polishReview is on (default off).
- Hidden fail:
  - card: 'Passes your checks but not count_words('a  b'): you return {'': 1, 'a': 1, 'b': 1}. What did you assume about the input?' It shows the call and their actual result, not the expected value.
  - records transfer evidence (wrong) on that spec's concept, and sets Task.spec.overfit = true
  - the task stays in building
NO SPECS, OR applicable = false: keep the manual Check my work button and the async review path.

v1Mechanisms.name: 12. Own-code probes: predict your function and what-if mutants (replaces explain-back)
v1Mechanisms.spec:
REQUIRES consent 'all' and a Python, JS or TS runtime.
PROBE INPUTS, in order of preference. The model writes only call expressions, never implementation code.
(1) Locally mutated spec inputs. Zero model cost.
    - Take a visible or hidden spec call and change one literal: a list or string to empty; an int to 0, -1 or a boundary such as len - 1; or a duplicated element.
    - Keep only mutations whose argument tuple differs from every visible spec's.
    - The expected value is never known in advance: the learner's own code is run to get it.
    - Spec calls themselves are never used. Visible titles and TestMessage.diff show their expected values, and hidden calls exist to catch hard-coding.
(2) Otherwise (no spec ladder), an OwnCodeProbeSchema job: low effort, bg priority 2.
    - Fired on save when the file's set of function symbols changed, at most once per 2 min, only during building.
    - Every callExpr goes through validateCall (mechanism 11).
(3) Local fallback inputs from parameter names: empty list or string, 0, -1, None/null.
FINDING FUNCTIONS: executeDocumentSymbolProvider (SymbolKind.Function and Method), with a fallback regex on def/function/const-arrow lines.
MODULE SAFETY: the same loader and top-level safety rules as mechanism 11 (Python: normal import under a non-main name, with the audit hook and the input/argv sentinels; JS: the top-level check). An unsafe module is skipped.
A. PREDICT YOUR FUNCTION:
- Offered through the tempo bar ('$(question) predict parse_row (15s)') and a gutter icon plus a hover command link on the def line. No CodeLens, so lines never jump.
- Shown only when the scheduler allows (a pause, at most once per 3 active min, never while stuck score is .5-1.0 except as the pre-hint step), or on Ctrl+Alt+P.
- Opens createInputBox:
  - title 'parse_row('a,,b') -> ?'
  - prompt 'Type the return value, or the error name. Enter submits'
  - validationMessage {message: 'Empty means no idea', severity: Info} while empty
  - ignoreFocusOut = true
  - buttons [{iconPath: ThemeIcon('history'), tooltip: 'Later'}]
  - Later or Esc is neutral.
- Accept runs the call against the CURRENT file text in about 300 ms (Python: probe.py with the source passed in; Node: dynamic import of a temp copy), then compares with compareOutput (mechanism 2) or the exception name.
- Feedback goes through the LineAnnotationManager on the def line: 'ok 9s' (green), or 'actual ['a', '', 'b'] · you said ['a', 'b']' (red). It clears on the next edit inside that function.
- Evidence: own-predict on the probe's concept, plus misconceptionIfWrong at x3 odds (unconfirmed).
- A mismatch whose concept has a cached atom queues an 'atom' offer.
- Pre-hint use: the result goes into the hint prompt. A match tells the model to look elsewhere; a mismatch is quoted word for word.
B. WHAT-IF MUTANTS:
- Run when criteria are met (spec ladder all green, or checkWork meetsCriteria). Skipped entirely when every task concept is Fluent.
- Pick 2 lines inside task functions that probe calls exercise. Prefer lines whose operator tag matches the task's weakest concept or a mistake already in the journal.
- Local operator table, with the misconception tag each maps to:
  - < <-> <=, > <-> >=: off-by-one
  - range bound or loop limit +/-1: for-range-bounds
  - drop 'return' on a return line: function-return-vs-print
  - and <-> or, && <-> ||: booleans-truthiness
  - .copy(), list(x), x[:], [...x] -> x: alias-copy
  - += -> =: loop-accumulator
  - remove await: await-sequencing
  - Python only, == -> is: identity-vs-equality
- Apply the operator to an in-memory copy and run the probe call.
  - Keep mutants whose result differs from the original; raising is a valid answer.
  - Drop mutants that fail to parse (py_compile or node --check).
- Display as decorations only; the file is never edited:
  - textDecoration 'line-through' on the changed token
  - after-text 'what if: range(len(prices) - 1)'
- InputBox (ignoreFocusOut = true, 'Later' button): 'With this change, total([4, 5, 6]) -> ?'.
- Grading and attribution:
  - A correct answer is own evidence: kind 'what-if', on the concept of the operator's tag.
  - A wrong answer counts toward the operator's misconception (x3) ONLY when it equals the unmutated output (the learner thinks the change does not matter), or the output under the specific alternative operator (computed locally).
  - Any other wrong answer is weight .5 wrong evidence on the concept, with no misconception, since tracing load or arithmetic can explain it.
- 2 what-ifs take about 30-60 s for a beginner. Then completeTask.
- CONFLICT FLAG: specs went green fast, but 2 or more own predictions were wrong in this task. Sets Task.notUnderstood = true:
  - what-ifs become 3
  - the next task's stuck threshold drops by 25%
  - one bg-graded explain question is added
  - Progress shows it neutrally
- FALLBACK when there is no runtime, consent or probe: the free-text explain-back, graded in the background (mechanism 9).

final.latencyStrategy:
PER-TASK CALL BUDGET (designed to 4 or fewer background calls per task; expected about 2.5)
- TaskBatch: 1 per milestone of 3-6 tasks (about 0.25 per task).
- TaskPrep (gate + spec ladder for up to 3 tasks): about 0.35, plus repair about 0.1.
- AtomPacks: only for tags with no seed template and for project concepts, 1-2 concepts per call. About 0.5 per task in the first project, falling towards 0 as the cross-project cache fills.
- HintLadder: up to about 0.7, from a reserved 4 per hour.
- Escalation lesson: only after a failed re-probe, about 0.2.
- Follow-up: only when the weakest P < 0.6 or a misconception is active, about 0.3.
- OwnCodeProbe: only for spec-less tasks, about 0.2.
- Polish review and misconception naming: off by default.
At about 4 tasks per hour this is 10-12 calls, plus at most 4 hint ladders: 14-16 against the default budget of 20. Background calls run without the priority service tier.

PREFETCH SCHEDULE
- t=0, Start:
  - PlanOutline (medium, about 40-70 s, priority 0).
  - Runtime detection and seed instantiation run locally (about 1-2 s).
  - No seed for the language: a probes-only seed pack (low, about 10-15 s plus compile time, priority 0). Neutral pseudocode items fill the wait.
- Plan lands:
  - TaskPrep for tasks 1-3 (medium, about 40-60 s, priority 1, neededBy = predicted end of placement).
  - AtomPacks for the non-seed concepts of tasks 1-3 (medium, about 30-40 s each, priority 1).
- Milestone k starts: TaskBatch for milestone k+1 (medium, priority 1).
- The second-to-last task of a trio enters building: TaskPrep for the next trio (priority 1), plus AtomPacks for their non-seed concepts.
- Re-probe fails: escalation lesson (low, about 10 s, priority 0). The second sibling item (20-40 s) covers the call.
- Stuck score reaches 0.6:
  - HintLadder rungs 1-3 (medium, priority 2, from the hint reserve, keyed per task, at most 4 per hour).
  - Without a spec ladder: OwnCodeProbe inputs (low, priority 2, at most 1 per 2 min).
- Criteria met: FollowUp, only if the weakest P < 0.6 or a misconception is active (medium, priority 1).
- Low stock (fewer than 3 unseen items) for a due, fragile, Fixing or misconception concept:
  - Seeded tags refill locally, with no call.
  - Other tags get a single-concept refill (low, priority 3).
- Usage-limit error (any provider): the background lane pauses for 15 min, queued speculative jobs are dropped, and the hourly budget halves for the session.

DEADLINES AND DEGRADED PATHS (priority-1 jobs carry neededBy)
- TaskPrep late at task start: show the interface card from the plan, skip the gate ('Plan it in your head'), and attach the specs when they land.
- AtomPack late when the gate routes to it: the gap becomes a JIT offer. If the learner presses Teach meanwhile, the foreground mini atom is used.
- TaskBatch late at milestone end: show a 'next milestone is being prepared' card with a sprint offer.
- HintLadder not prefetched: on-demand call at low effort, about 10-15 s.

GRADED LOCALLY (never waits on a model)
- Placement items; atom predict, completion, contrast and traceback items; belief checks; refutation re-probes; sprints and which-pattern picks.
- Gate pattern and plan picks.
- Spec runs on save, failure-signature nudges, hidden-spec checks and JIT offers.
- Own-code predictions and what-if mutants.
- Paste and assisted-insert detection, all evidence and BKT maths, scheduling, propagation, audits and tempo decisions.
- Execution cost, measured here:
  - one Python spawn: about 96 ms with the real exe
  - Node: about 80 ms; Node with .ts: about 130 ms
  - a verification batch: about 0.3-0.8 s per pass
  - a spec run with light imports: about 150-400 ms for Python, 100-300 ms for Node
  - completion grading in compiled languages: 1-2 s

STILL MODEL-JUDGED, BUT IN THE BACKGROUND (results arrive as a log card plus evidence)
- 'I'd do it differently' / the free-text plan.
- The explain-back fallback, used only when there is no runtime.
- Follow-up design.
- Polish review and naming of unmatched wrong answers (both opt-in).

STILL BLOCKS ON A MODEL (foreground, rare)
- Ask the coach and Reveal.
- Teach on a concept with no seed and no cached or in-flight pack: a mini atom at low effort, about 20-30 s including verification. (The earlier 10-15 s estimate ignored Codex start-up, output size and verification.) A sprint fills the wait only when the learner is not building.
- A hint on a prefetch miss: low effort, about 10-15 s (was 20-40 s at medium).
- Check my work for spec-less tasks: medium effort, about 30-40 s. It runs async, and the learner keeps coding.

TARGET WAITS
- Atom, placement, sprint, gate, belief-check and traceback feedback: under 300 ms.
- Completion grading: under 1 s for Python/JS/TS, 1-2 s for compiled languages.
- Spec verdict after a manual save: under 1 s with light imports; otherwise 'running specs...' is shown.
- Start to first placement item: 2 s or less for Python/JS/TS; other languages get neutral items immediately.
- Start to first keystroke in task 1: 4 min or less.
- Hint rungs 1-3: 0 s when prefetched (target: at least 70% of served rungs); 15 s or less on a miss.
- Task end to next task: 0 s when TaskPrep is on time (target: 10% or fewer priority-1 deadline misses).
- Learner-visible model wait per task: 5 s or less median.
- Any wait over 3 s that the learner started outside building is filled with a sprint. During building a sprint is offered, never forced.
final.learnerModelChanges:
ONE ENTRY POINT
- Every gap signal becomes an Evidence record passed to recordEvidence().
- Each record is appended to a JSONL log, which is the source of truth.
- ConceptState.mastery stores P(known), so stuckThreshold, weakest, the Progress bars and every prompt keep working.

NO SINGLE ITEM DECIDES
- The likelihood ratio of any one update is capped at 6.
- Predict items take their guess rate from the answer space: boolean .5, small integer .2, structured .06 (raised to the cap).
- P stays at or below .8 until the concept has all of:
  - correct non-guess answers from 2 sibling groups
  - a production item (a completion, or a cleanly earned spec green)
  - coverage of its common misconceptions
- Worked example: one correct predict moves P from .30 to .734; two reach the .8 cap; a passing completion then gives .962 and mastery.
- Downward evidence is limited too:
  - one wrong answer caps only direct children
  - '?' and flagged guesses count at half weight
  - an empty submit is never scored
- A delayed production audit (in a sprint, 1+ day later) re-checks every mastered concept. A miss revokes mastery.

HOW EACH DIAGNOSIS SOURCE FEEDS THE MODEL
- Wrong prediction that matches an executed mutant:
  - The learner is asked 'Did you think <belief>? y/n'.
  - y: misconception odds x6, and the mutant's precision count rises. Then an active contrast pick, a reveal (with a Python state trace for semantics tags), and a re-probe on another surface.
  - n: treated as a slip: half-weight wrong evidence, no misconception update.
  - Never names a belief for: the bare answer 'error', answers within edit distance 1 of the actual output, or ambiguous mutant outputs.
  - In placement the match is stored unconfirmed (x3 for curated mutants, x2 for model mutants), and the later atom starts from it.
- Misconception lifecycle:
  - candidate on the first match
  - active with matches from 2+ sibling groups
  - suppressed after an immediate correct re-probe: still scheduled, still blocks mastery, named in prompts as Fixing
  - cleared after 2 delayed hits: 10+ min later in an unlabelled interleaved sprint, then 1+ day later
  - a later match is a relapse
- Wrong prediction with no mutant match, or '?': both take the same UNKNOWN path, so honesty is never slower than guessing. Optional background naming of the belief is off by default.
- Format-only answers ('hi' with quotes, a tuple written as a list): no evidence, just a one-line format note.
- Completion failure: wrong production evidence. A fill equal to a tagged wrongFill names that misconception (x3).
- Correct but slow (over 2x par_self, after the first 15 items): Fragile.
- Correct but guess-flagged (explicitly, or inferred from very fast latency or a copied literal): counted, with P capped at .8 and one interleaved item scheduled. Not Fragile.
- Traceback items: the line and exception name are graded locally, plus the meaning pick, on the 'reading-tracebacks' concept.
- Gate pattern pick:
  - A missed required pattern is recognition evidence (guess .3).
  - A lure pick is weight .3 wrong evidence with no misconception.
- Flawed plan pick: wrong on flawConceptId, with misconception odds x2. Repeated across 3 tasks, it lowers 'decomposition'.
- Specs:
  - The first green is production evidence, at full weight only within 3 saves and without assisted inserts.
  - A failure-signature match is passive misconception evidence (x1.5, weight .5). It never activates a misconception on its own.
  - Visible specs green with hidden specs red is a transfer failure and flags 'overfit'.
- Own-code prediction:
  - A mismatch is wrong evidence plus misconceptionIfWrong (x3, unconfirmed). A match is correct evidence.
  - Fast greens combined with 2+ wrong own predictions set Task.notUnderstood.
- What-if mutant: a wrong answer counts against the operator's misconception only if it equals the unmutated output or the alternative operator's output. Otherwise it is half-weight wrong evidence on the concept.
- Hints: rung 1 at weight .3; rungs 2-5 at weight .5 (model diagnoses are not decisive); reveal at weight 1.
- Paste (120+ characters equal to the clipboard) and assisted inserts (40+ net-new characters not from the clipboard):
  - add to the task's pasted or assisted characters
  - lower spec evidence on that function to weight .3
  - count against an unaided solve
- Task solve: 'task' evidence by maximum rung, reveal, paste and assist. Solo tasks also update 'decomposition' at full weight.
- Model grades (background explain-back, free-text plan): guess .2, slip .2, weight .5.

GRAPH AND PATTERNS
- Prerequisite propagation (cycle-checked, at most 3 hops):
  - An ancestor becomes inferred-mastered (P .9) only with support from 2+ tested descendants, one of them with production evidence.
  - Support from a single descendant gives at most .75.
  - Inferred-mastered concepts skip gates and are audited first.
- Concept aliases merge plan ids into seed ids by tag, so placement evidence is never orphaned.
- Pattern Deck: each atom exit adds or updates a PatternCard under its canonical name, with 6+ use cases (shape concepts: a template; semantics concepts: a rule). Deck names feed the gate options and which-pattern items; distractors come from tags that are not valid alternatives.
- selectionGap: a concept answered correctly in an atom but wrong when interleaved gets which-pattern and contrast practice.
- Fluency is measured against par_abs: reading time + the learner's own typing speed + unscaled thinking time. Fluent therefore means fast thinking, regardless of typing speed. Fluent concepts:
  - skip gates and what-ifs
  - get maximum stuck rope (1.5)
  - appear only in long-interval sprints
- Decomposition P drives scaffold fading (mechanism 8), and solo tasks measure it directly.

SCHEDULING AND SELECTION BY STATE
- Misconception (active or Fixing): a delayed check at 10 min (interleaved, unlabelled), then at .25 day and 1 day until cleared.
- Fragile: 10 min, then 1 day.
- Guess-flagged correct: one interleaved item this session.
- Solid: interval x2.2, plus one delayed production audit.
- Follow-up tasks only when the weakest P < .6 or a misconception is active.
- The coach never starts atoms for Solid or Fluent concepts.

MIGRATION, PERSISTENCE AND LOGGING
- Existing profiles keep mastery as their P prior. New fields get defaults, with tested = attempts > 0.
- Evidence lives in globalStorageUri/evidence-YYYY-MM.jsonl. globalState keeps compact summaries, merged per concept before each write, so two windows never erase each other's progress.
- The log keeps every observation, with the bits of information each item carried. This lets the guess, slip, learning-rate and par parameters, and mutant precision, be refitted locally later.

final.successMetrics:
All metrics are computed locally from the evidence log, per-task timestamps and job stats. They are shown in a 'Pace' section of the Progress tab, and nothing is sent anywhere.

HEADLINE (transfer speed, which scaffolded tasks cannot fake)
- Solo tasks (one per milestone, no gate, no titles, hints capped at rung 2), tracked for:
  - active minutes
  - unaided solve rate: no rung 2+ hint, no reveal, pasted + assisted characters under 120
  Both should improve milestone over milestone.
- Active minutes per milestone at fixed scope, and learner-visible model wait seconds per milestone. These replace 'tasks per hour', which mostly measured that tasks got 3x smaller.

SPEED
- Start to first keystroke in task 1: median 4 min or less (today about 10-15 min).
- Model wait on the critical path: 5 s or less median per task (today about 3-5 min).
- Concept block time p50 (today 4-6 min per lesson plus its check):
  - known concept: 30 s or less
  - misconception: 70 s or less
  - unknown concept: 120 s or less
- Words read per concept block: 60 or fewer. Escalation lessons are excluded and counted separately.
- Overhead per task (gate + pre-build atoms + what-ifs): median 90 s or less, falling across milestones as fading removes steps.
- Hint rungs 1-3 served from the prefetch: 70% or more.
- Placement: 14 items or fewer, 3 min or less, zero GradeSchema calls.

DEPTH AND DIAGNOSIS
- Information per task: median evidence bits per task (the sum of KL divergence from prior to posterior), reported instead of event counts. Low-information events such as pattern picks and spec greens count only for what they are worth.
- Misconception attribution:
  - coverage (share of wrong predictions matched to a mutant), reported next to precision (y-confirmation rate of belief checks, target 70% or more)
  - mutants below 30% precision after 5 asks are retired automatically
- False mastery: under 10% of delayed production audits fail. Audits are random, 1+ day after mastery, include inferred concepts, and do not depend on whether a task happened to use the concept.
- Refutation:
  - 70% or more of confirmed refutations are followed by a correct re-probe on a different surface
  - relapse within 7 days is 20% or less, measured by the delayed checks that keep running while a misconception is suppressed
- Retention, on fresh instances (never an exact repeat): 80% or more correct on sprint items for mastered concepts after 1+ day, and 70% or more after 7+ days.
- Calibration: non-guess accuracy is at least 30 points above guess-flagged accuracy. Flag usage (explicit + implicit) is tracked so the stat is never empty.
- The format-only answer rate falls over the first sessions.
- Traceback item accuracy rises, and the time from a persistent project error to the next progress event falls.

THE LEARNER DOES THE WORK
- Share of active time spent writing project code: 70% or more. Sprints and atoms together: 25% or less, with sprints alone at 15% or less.
- Pasted + assisted characters per task trend down. Reveal rate is 1 or fewer per 10 tasks.
- Own-code prediction accuracy rises across tasks. Conflict flags and overfit flags fall.

COST AND HEALTH
- Background calls: 4 or fewer per task and 20 or fewer per hour. At about 4 tasks per hour the design expects 14-16, including hints.
- Priority-1 deadline misses: 10% or less.
- Verification pass rate: 85% or more of model items. Seed instance validity: 95% or more.
- Prefetched content actually used: 60% or more.
- Skip/Esc rate per nudge kind: under 30%. A higher rate means the nudge interrupts too much and its scheduler limits should tighten.
- Tracked as regression signals:
  - learners who switch localExecution or proactiveHints to 'off'
  - learners who decline the inline-AI offer and then show high assisted counts

issues.issue: A single predict item marks a concept mastered. With P=.30, g=.03 and s=.10, one correct, unflagged, on-par predict gives P=.928 (the spec's own test value). That is at or above .85, so PROBE exits 'tested-out' and isMastered is true (tested, not fragile, no active misconception). From then on the concept 'costs 0 in gates and is never re-taught'. Three things are wrong with this. (a) The likelihood ratio of a correct answer is .9/.03 = 30, which is not credible for model-written 8-line items of unknown difficulty, many of which print a small integer. (b) A predict item tests reading and tracing only; nothing checks that the learner can write the pattern, so production misconceptions such as writing xs[i:i+n-1] slip through. (c) One probe only exercises the 1-3 mutants it carries, while a concept like list-slicing has 4-5 common misconceptions (end-exclusive, negative indices, out-of-range slices do not raise, a slice is a copy, step).
issues.fix: Make 'tested-out' require at least 2 correct items from 2 different sibling groups, and require one of them to be a production item: a completion, or the first green spec on that concept. Together the items must carry mutants for every taxonomy misconception of the tag with prior >= .2. Until then, cap P at .8. Raise g for predict to .12 (.2 when the output is a single integer under 20 or a boolean). Cap the likelihood ratio of any single item at 6. Add a delayed audit: each mastered concept gets one production item in a sprint 1 or more days later, and a miss there revokes mastery.

issues.issue: The pad leaks its answers. It is a real atom.py/.js/.ts file. Copilot and other inline-suggestion providers will show ghost text on the '# -> ' line and in completion blanks, and they are good at predicting print output. The Python and JS extensions also show a Run button for the file, and Pylance hovers show types. A learner can get every probe 'correct' without noticing they were helped, and with g=.03 each such answer counts as near-proof of mastery.
issues.fix: Open the pad under a custom language id: contribute 'deliberate-pad-python', '-js' and '-ts', and switch with vscode.languages.setTextDocumentLanguage (present in the 1.93 typings). Give each a tiny grammar that includes source.python or source.js, so syntax colouring still works but no language server, Run button or diagnostics attach. Contribute configurationDefaults for those language ids: editor.inlineSuggest.enabled false, editor.quickSuggestions off, editor.suggestOnTriggerCharacters false, editor.hover.enabled false. First verify that each of these settings is language-overridable. Also discard (do not count) any answer submitted within 1.5 s of a multi-character insert in the pad that was not typed.

issues.issue: Typed-answer grading confuses output format with understanding and hides a real misconception. (1) Python print(['a','b']) shows ['a', 'b']. A beginner typing [a, b] or a, b is marked wrong with s=.05, so P drops from .30 to .02 and the concept's descendants are capped at .27. One formatting slip reads as 'knows nothing'. (2) print('hi') shows hi, so a learner who types 'hi' with quotes is wrong. (3) Tuples, sets and dicts with int keys do not parse as JSON, so a spacing difference fails the exact string compare. (4) A bug: JSON.parse('3.0') === JSON.parse('3'), so for 6/2 in Python the answer '3' is graded correct against the real '3.0'. The whole integer-division and int-float misconception class (the canonical tags numbers-int-float and integer-division-modulo) can never be detected, and the '/ gives an int' mutant is either dropped or never matched. (5) Replacing single quotes with double quotes corrupts strings that contain apostrophes.
issues.fix: Normalise in the target language. For Python, run a resident normaliser process that uses ast.literal_eval on both sides and compares type-preserving reprs: int and float differ, tuple and list differ. For JS, use a JSON5-tolerant parser that keeps the number formatting text when the concept tag is numeric. Add a third verdict, 'format-only', for answers that match after removing quotes and brackets or after converting between tuple and list. That verdict records no evidence and shows 'right idea; Python writes it as ["a", "b"]', unless the concept's mutants differ exactly in that format. When verifying mutants, drop a mutant only when it is equal to the original under the strict comparison, not under the loose one.

issues.issue: Misconceptions found in placement are never refuted, and the routing contradicts the design. A committed wrong placement answer that matches a mutant drops P to .022 (spec test value). ROUTE sends any concept with P < .15 straight to UNKNOWN (worked example, completion, predict). So exactly the learners whose specific belief was diagnosed get a generic example rather than the 12 s refutation of that belief. The REFUTE path is reachable only when the misconception first appears inside an atom.
issues.fix: Route by misconception before P. If any misconception on the concept has p >= .3, start at REFUTE(M) and then re-probe on a fresh group. Use UNKNOWN only when there is no misconception evidence and P < .15 or the learner answered don't-know.

issues.issue: A misconception clears after one cued, immediate re-probe, so it never gets a durable test. The odds for M go from .15 x6 to p=.51 on the first match. A correct re-probe seconds later, straight after the learner read '# Rule: <rule>', applies x.25 and gives p=.21. That is below .3, so M becomes inactive. The re-probe tests short-term application of a rule just stated about the same feature, not a changed belief. Because M is now inactive, it no longer drives scheduling, so the 10-minute and same-day re-checks never fire. The metric '20% or fewer of fixed misconceptions come back within 7 days' will look good because the system stopped looking.
issues.fix: Split 'suppressed' from 'cleared'. An immediate re-probe sets M to suppressed: p is lowered but it still schedules. Clearing needs a correct, non-guess answer on an item carrying M's mutant, at least 10 minutes later, inside an interleaved sprint whose header does not name the concept. A second one at least 1 day later clears M fully. clearHits counts only those delayed hits.

issues.issue: The coach states the belief as fact on a single match, even though matches are often coincidental. The pad says '# You expected <belief>.' after one mutant match. Many probes print small integers, and mutants usually move the output by ±1. A careless arithmetic slip, a typo, or the generic answer 'error' against a mutant that raises will often equal a mutant output. Two mutants on one probe can also print the same thing, and the spec never checks for that. Telling a learner they hold a belief they do not hold wastes the 12 s, costs trust, and can plant the misconception. The 'belief in the learner's words' is really the model's paraphrase.
issues.fix: (1) In verification, drop or merge mutants whose outputs equal each other, and prefer probes whose outputs are high-entropy (lists or strings rather than one small int). (2) Never match the bare answer 'error' to a mutant; require the exception name. (3) Turn the refutation into a one-key confirmation: '# Did you think <belief>? y/n'. Yes multiplies the odds by 6 and refutes. No treats the answer as a slip (no misconception update, wrong evidence with s .15) and shows only 'actual: X'. The confirmation rate also gives you a precision measure for each mutant.

issues.issue: The refutation is passive. Its learning content is about 12 s of reading: belief, wrong snippet with output, right snippet with output, rule. Beginners skim passive contrast text. Also, belief (15 words) + refutation (40) + rule (15) is 70 words, which already breaks the 60-word budget, and that excludes the code. Realistic reading time for a beginner is 20-30 s, not 12.
issues.fix: Make the contrast active and graded locally. Show both snippets without outputs and ask 'Which one prints [2, 3]? 1/2' (one key, about 3 s, guess .5), then reveal both outputs. For Python state misconceptions (alias-copy, loop-accumulator, scope), add a sys.settrace pass over the 8-line probe at verification time and show each line's variable values as after-text. That way the refutation shows the program state step by step instead of a sentence. This is a small V1 slice of v2 item 4. Cut the refutation to 25 words so the total stays under 60.

issues.issue: The probe header names the concept ('# list slicing · what does this print?'). This hands the learner the deciding question, 'which idea applies here?', and turns every item into 'apply the slicing rule'. In sprints it also cancels the interleaving that selectionGap relies on, so selectionGap will rarely fire. In re-probes it inflates the 'fixed' rate.
issues.fix: Use a generic header ('# what does this print?') for placement, re-probes, final predicts and all sprint items. Show the concept name only in the exit flash and the log card. Keep named headers only for the UNKNOWN worked example.

issues.issue: The rule that a probe prints exactly one line excludes the most common beginner control-flow and indentation misconceptions. Examples: print inside versus after the loop, the order of nested loops, a return inside a loop body, while-loop iteration counts, and JS console.log ordering around await and setTimeout. These need more than one line of output to show. None of them will ever be detected or refuted. Separately, a single scalar print hides type: print('5') and print(5) both show 5, so string-versus-number confusion, such as input() returning a str, never shows up.
issues.fix: Allow 1-4 output lines. Accept answers on several '# -> ' lines, or space- or comma-separated on one line, and compare line by line after normalising. For type-sensitive tags, require the probe to print repr(x) or type(x).__name__ (Python) or JSON.stringify or typeof (JS). Add a verification check that a str mutant and an int mutant produce different output.

issues.issue: Probes mix in other concepts. An 8-line list-slicing probe may use a for loop, an f-string or a comprehension the beginner has never seen. The wrong answer is charged to slicing (s .05, so P drops to .02), and the propagation step then caps every descendant of slicing at .27. Nothing in the AtomPack prompt or in verification limits which constructs a probe may use.
issues.fix: Give each tag a 'constructs used' signature, checked locally: a Python ast walk, or for JS a token and regex table. Pass the learner's set of constructs with P >= .6 into the AtomPack prompt as the allowed list. At selection time, skip probes that use a construct with P < .5 other than the target, falling back to a probe that is free of such confounds. Tag the seed probes the same way.

issues.issue: The incentives teach the learner to hide uncertainty. The learner's stated aim is speed. Pressing Ctrl+Shift+Enter on a correct answer marks the concept Fragile, which blocks mastery for at least 1 hour and causes more gates, atoms and sprint items. Typing '?' always sends them down the 60-90 s UNKNOWN path. A blind guess costs the same time as an honest 'don't know' when wrong and saves about 60 s when right. So the rational speed-seeking strategy is to never flag and always guess. That is exactly the behaviour g=.03 assumes away, and the calibration metric will be empty.
issues.fix: Do not charge time for honesty. A guess-flagged correct answer counts as correct with P capped at .8 and schedules one interleaved item, rather than setting Fragile on the spot. Infer guessing automatically as well: latency under 0.3 x par, or an answer copied from the probe's literals, sets an implicit guess flag. Show the calibration score as a visible stat so the honest flag has a payoff.

issues.issue: The item banks run out, and memorised answers inflate the metrics. An atom has 4 probes in 'at least 2' sibling groups. One path through the step machine can need 4-5 distinct unseen groups: placement, PROBE, RE-PROBE, a second sibling, the final UNKNOWN predict, and later sprints and clear-hits. Seed banks hold about 20 fundamentals x 4 probes and are reused across placement, atoms and every sprint. Learners will remember outputs, so the retention and 'fixed' metrics will measure memory of strings, and refill calls are priority 3, the first to be dropped under the budget.
issues.fix: Make the seed fundamentals parametric. Each seed probe becomes a template with typed slots (list contents, indices, names, story nouns), and the local runner records outputs for fresh instances. Mutants become local program transforms tied to misconception ids, as in mechanism 12's operator table. That gives unlimited surface isomorphs at zero model cost, with trusted belief labels. For model packs, require 4 probes in 4 groups. Never reuse an exact item within 7 days.

issues.issue: Execution does not verify that a mutant represents its belief. Running a mutant only proves that it prints something different. Whether the change actually encodes 'the belief' is still the model's claim. Worse, step 2 overwrites the model's claimed answer with the real output. When the two differ, the model misunderstood its own item, so its mutants, belief text and refutation (which may quote numbers) were written from a wrong mental model. Example: Python 'a = 1000; b = 1000; print(a is b)' prints True inside one script because the constants are folded, which contradicts a refutation saying 'is checks identity, so this is False'.
issues.fix: In verification, if sameOutput(modelAnswer, realOutput) fails, send the probe for repair or drop it; never overwrite it. Ban numbers and quoted outputs in refutation text, and build the 'actual: X, you said: Y' line locally from real outputs. Give model-written mutants odds x3 instead of x6 until a learner confirms them (see the y/n step). Hand-curated operator mutants for seed tags keep x6.

issues.issue: Deferred gaps are left to stuck detection, which takes minutes. Only 2 atoms are allowed before building; 'any other gap waits for the hint path'. With stuckMinutes defaulting to 7 and stuckThreshold = 7 x (.6 + .9P), a concept at P .02-.30 reaches score 1.0 only after 4.3-6.1 active minutes without progress. Rung 2, which is what queues the atom, needs about 0.75 x that again. So the learner flounders for about 7-10 minutes on a gap the system already knew about, inside a task sized at 5-15 minutes. That is slower than today's up-front lesson.
issues.fix: Offer deferred atoms just in time, not through stuck detection. When the next red spec's conceptId (or a gate-missed pattern's concept) has P < .5, show 'next: <spec> uses <pattern> - 60 s drill? Alt+N' in the tempo bar the moment that spec becomes the next one. Also offer it on the first save that touches the function under that spec. Keep the hint path only for gaps nobody predicted.

issues.issue: 'Faster end to end' is claimed by timing pieces that are not realistic, and partly by changing units. The gate takes far longer than stated. Step A means reading 6-7 items of about 20 words each (roughly 120 words), toggling with Space, then a feedback QuickPick. Step B means reading 3 plans of 25 words each plus feedback. For a beginner that is 45-75 s, not 13-22 s, and it is not counted in the 60-word budget. Add up to 2 atoms (capped at 120 s) and 2 what-ifs on their own code (about 15-30 s each for a beginner), and the overhead is 2.5-4 minutes on a task now sized at 5-15 minutes, or 25-45%. 'Tasks per hour 3-5 vs 1' only reflects tasks being 3x smaller. Per hour, the gate overhead may well grow compared with today's single gate on a 15-45 minute task.
issues.fix: Run the gate per milestone, or only when a task brings in a concept not exercised by the previous task; consecutive tasks share concepts. Count gate words in the reading budget, with a cap of about 50: drop the detail lines and show useWhen only for missed items. Skip what-ifs when every task concept is Fluent. Replace 'tasks/hour' with minutes of active time per milestone at fixed scope, plus learner-visible wait seconds per milestone.

issues.issue: The background budget cannot sustain the promised pace, so the 0 s waits fail exactly where they matter. Per task the design enqueues: a TaskGate call (about half a call), a SpecLadder (plus a repair about 30% of the time), AtomPacks (1-3 calls for non-seed concepts), a HintLadder (0-2), OwnCodeProbe, escalation lessons (up to 2, fired on the first match because p crosses .5 after one x6 update), a follow-up, polish review, MisconceptionGuess enrichment and refills. That is about 6-10 calls per task. At the target of 3-5 tasks an hour, that is 18-50 calls an hour against a cap of 20. Priority-1 jobs then queue, so 'task end to next task: 0 s' and 'hint rungs 70% prefetched' fail on the default settings, and sustained medium-effort usage risks ChatGPT plan limits mid-session.
issues.fix: Publish a per-task call budget of 4 or fewer and design to it. (1) Put the per-task interface and spec ladder for the first 3 tasks into one call made right after the plan (or into the plan schema itself). (2) Request AtomPacks only for tags with no seed. (3) Fire the escalation lesson only when the RE-PROBE fails; the second sibling item gives about 20-40 s, enough for a low-effort call of about 10 s. (4) Turn polish review and enrichment off by default. (5) Simulate an hour of usage in test/jobs.test.ts and assert priority-1 queue wait is 30 s or less.

issues.issue: The spec ladder's interface can arrive after the learner has started coding. Task 1's SpecLadder (medium, about 30 s, plus verification and possible repair) is enqueued only once the plan lands, about 100-150 s in. The gate cache-miss path tells the learner to start building at once. If they have already written def count(words): and the ladder then lands requiring count_words(text) -> dict in a different file, the specs go red for reasons unrelated to the concept. Evidence, stuck detection and signature nudges are then all wrong.
issues.fix: Fix each task's interface (file and 1-3 signatures) in the PlanSchema output, and make SpecLadder conform to it. If the ladder has not landed when the task starts, show the interface card anyway and attach the specs when they arrive. If the learner has already diverged, map the specs to their names via executeDocumentSymbolProvider and signature arity, or mark the ladder not applicable rather than forcing a rename.

issues.issue: Decomposition, the main skill a beginner lacks after syntax, is never practised in V1, and nothing fades the scaffolding. Pattern pick hands over the required patterns, plan pick shows the workable plan, the spec titles list the behaviours simplest-first, and tasks are pre-cut to 5-15 minutes. Recognising a plan is not the same as producing one. The learner can become fast inside these scaffolds and stall on the first unscaffolded problem. Advanced learners pay the scaffolding cost on every task (expertise reversal). Fading appears only in v2 (items 1 and 10).
issues.fix: Put a fading rule in V1, driven by the 'decomposition' pseudo-concept P. Below .5: full gate and all spec titles. .5-.8: no plan pick; show only the next spec title and reveal later titles as each turns green. At .8 or above: interface plus hidden specs only, with tasks growing to 20-30 minutes. At every milestone, run one 'solo task': no gate, no titles, hints capped at rung 2. That gives an honest transfer measure; report its time and unaided-solve rate as the headline speed metric.

issues.issue: The evidence from the learner's project code is unreliable. Paste detection compares inserts with the clipboard, so Copilot or IntelliCode inline completions, which arrive as single large edits, count as typed. Specs that turn green within 2x par then record correct 'spec' evidence (P .30 to .72 per spec), and recordSolve counts the task as unaided. Trial-and-error edits until a TestMessage.diff turns green also count as understanding.
issues.fix: Treat any single content change of 40 or more non-whitespace characters with reason undefined, not equal to the clipboard and not a snippet insert as 'assisted'. Add it to pastedChars and cap spec evidence on that function at weight .3. Offer once, with consent, to set editor.inlineSuggest.enabled false for the workspace during tasks. Count a spec green as correct only when the number of saves since it went red is 3 or fewer; more saves than that is tinkering, recorded as weight .3.

issues.issue: The UNKNOWN path is too thin for concepts that are not atom-sized, and the caps cut off the escalation. For a true beginner meeting def, return, classes and instances, recursion, closures, generators or async/await, a 15 s look at a 5-8 line example, one completion and one predict cannot build a usable mental model. Worked-example research generally needs 2 or more varied examples before learners generalise. The ESCALATE lesson (120 words, about 40-60 s for a beginner) plus a fresh completion usually comes after about 150 s, which is exactly the hard cap of 7 items or 150 s. So the deepest remedy is the one most often cut off.
issues.fix: Mark tags as 'large' in tags.ts: functions, classes-instances, recursion-base-case, closures, generators-iteration, async-await-promises, this-binding. Split each into 2-4 sub-atoms in the DAG; for example, recursion becomes base case, then the call stack, then combining results. For large tags, UNKNOWN shows 2 worked examples on different surfaces and then a faded completion (1 blank, then 2). Exempt ESCALATE from the 150 s cap, or start the cap's clock after the first refutation.

issues.issue: Setting P from the learner's ticks inverts the selection rule and does not spare advanced learners. The placement score uses (1 - |P - .5| x 2). Ticking 'used' sets P to .5, which maximises uncertainty, so every ticked fundamental is probed first. An expert who ticks all 8 gets 8 basic items, including variables-assignment. Upward propagation is capped at .8 x P, so ancestors can never reach .85, and every inferred fundamental then needs a separate confirmation item in later gates. Advanced learners get easy items repeatedly.
issues.fix: Placement should start at DAG leaves for ticked concepts. One correct, unflagged leaf item with no mutant match, plus a production item on another leaf, should set the inferred ancestors to mastered with P .9 (not capped at .8). Self-ticks should set P to .7 and pick items near the leaves. Add an 'experienced' fast lane: 3 correct leaves in a row under par ends placement and skips gates for anything inferred.

issues.issue: Model-written gate keys penalise valid alternative approaches as misconceptions. 'Lure selected: wrong, misconception taken from whyNot.' The lures come from a low-effort model call told to write near-misses, and nothing verifies them. Valid alternatives are common: collections.Counter versus dict.get, sort-then-group versus a dict, a set for uniqueness and then counting. Choosing one records a named misconception that then appears in every prompt. The 1-of-3 plan pick has the usual test-taking cues of model-written options; the workable plan tends to be the longest and most specific, so the effective guess rate is above .33.
issues.fix: Record no misconception from lure picks; at most, wrong evidence at weight .3. Plan-pick misconception odds should be x2, not x6. Add a QuickPick button 'I'd do it differently', which defers to the background explain path with no penalty. Shuffle the plans and require the 3 to be within ±20% of each other in length; check this locally and drop the gate if it fails.

issues.issue: What-if and hint evidence charges errors to the wrong cause. A wrong what-if answer on '< changed to <=' is counted toward off-by-one, but predicting a mutated version of your own 15-line function with [4, 5, 6] can fail through tracing load or arithmetic with no off-by-one belief at all. Hint-rung evidence (rung 2 counts as wrong with s .15 at weight 1) lands on whichever concept the model guessed; one model diagnosis moves a mastered concept from .93 to .67. Rung 1 is treated as 'a slip, record nothing', which assumes Socratic questions only fix slips.
issues.fix: For what-ifs, attribute to the operator's misconception only when the answer equals the unmutated output (the learner thinks the change does not matter) or the output under the specific alternative operator. Otherwise record weight .5 wrong evidence on the concept only. Hint-derived evidence gets weight .5, the same as llm-grade. Rung 1 records weak wrong evidence (weight .3).

issues.issue: Debugging and error reading, the skills that decide whether someone programs fast, are neither taught nor measured. There is no item type for reading a traceback or stack trace, finding the failing line, or telling a runtime error from a logic error. Diagnostics in the pad are suppressed, hints arrive already prepared, and environment problems are fixed directly by the coach. A beginner who leaves Deliberate will still lose most of their time to errors they cannot read.
issues.fix: Add a 'traceback' item kind graded locally. Run a seed snippet that raises, show the real trace in the pad, and ask for the line number and exception name, with a pick of 3 for the meaning. Generate these for free from the raising mutants the verifier already runs. In sprints, interleave them at 1 in 5. For persistent errors in project code, make rung 1 ask 'Which line does the trace point at, and what does <ExceptionName> mean?' before any content hint.

issues.issue: The latency and par bootstrap make beginners Fragile everywhere. speedFactor starts at 1 and only adapts after about 20 correct items. parSec values are model guesses of 8-15 s, but a beginner typing ['a', 'b', 'c'] needs 8-10 s for the typing alone. Early correct answers often exceed 2x par, which sets Fragile. Fragile blocks mastery and needs a correct answer at least 1 hour later to clear, so early tasks get extra gates and atoms purely from typing speed.
issues.fix: Compute par locally as read time (lines x ~1.5 s) plus type time (answer characters / the learner's measured characters per second) plus think time (the model's parSec, cut to 3-8 s). Measure characters per second with a first placement item that just asks the learner to copy a short literal. Do not set Fragile from latency during the first 15 items.

issues.issue: Pattern-first framing fits shape concepts but not semantics concepts, and the Pattern Deck will drift. alias-copy, scope-local-global, booleans-truthiness, identity-vs-equality and callbacks-event-loop are rules about how the program runs, not code shapes. Forcing a <holes> template on them teaches recipes without the underlying model. Each pattern has only 2 useCases, so which-pattern sprint items get memorised. Pattern names come from separate model calls and will be inconsistent ('Count with dict.get' versus 'Tally in a dictionary'), which makes the 4-option picks ambiguous.
issues.fix: Tag each concept as 'shape' or 'semantics'. Semantics atoms get a state-trace refutation and a 'rule' card instead of a template. Store canonical pattern names in the tag taxonomy, and require AtomPack and TaskGate to use them exactly; check locally and rename on mismatch. Require at least 6 useCases per pattern, never repeat a useCase within 7 days, and make sure the distractors in which-pattern items come from tags not marked as alternatives to the right one.

issues.issue: The surface is heavy for a true beginner, and help is hidden in hovers. The design asks a VS Code novice to manage Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+Shift+Enter, '?', Esc, Tab between placeholders, Alt+N, Ctrl+Alt+H, Ctrl+Alt+P, Ctrl+Alt+S, Space-to-toggle QuickPicks, the Testing view and CodeLens. Hint text is cut to 52 characters of after-text, with the full text only in a hover that beginners will not discover. The key legend shows only for the first 3 atoms. Opening a sprint automatically while the learner waits on Check my work also takes focus away from their code mid-thought, and can add up to 15 s after the review lands.
issues.fix: Show hints of more than 52 characters in a Comments API thread anchored on the line (createCommentController exists in 1.93) instead of hover-only after-text; this pulls v2 item 6 forward. Keep the key legend in the header until the learner has used each key 3 times. Never open a sprint automatically while the task phase is building; offer it in the tempo bar instead. On a hidden-spec failure, show the failing call itself, since the task is effectively done and a title alone gives a beginner nothing to debug.

issues.issue: The completion harness can be passed by gaming it. Verification checks that empty blanks fail and that the listed wrongFills fail, but not that a hard-coded fill (the expected literal, or 'return 6') fails. A model-written harness with a single assert will accept a constant.
issues.fix: Require harnesses to call the pattern code with at least 2 different inputs, and wrap completions in a function. In verify.ts, also try the expected output literal as a constant fill for each blank, and drop the completion if that passes.

issues.issue: The success metrics reward the failure modes described above. '50% or more of wrong predictions mapped to a named misconception' rewards over-attribution from output collisions. '15+ evidence events per task' counts low-information events such as pattern picks (g .3) and spec greens (g .15). 'False mastery' is measured by later rung-2 hints, which depend on the model's diagnosis and never fire for falsely mastered concepts that no task happens to use.
issues.fix: Report mutant-attribution precision (the y/n confirmation rate) next to coverage. Count evidence in expected bits (KL divergence from prior to posterior), not in events. Measure false mastery with the random delayed production audit from the first fix. Also report the solo-task unaided solve rate and time per milestone as the headline numbers.

issues.issue: Spec runs on every save (mech 11) execute the learner's real code with full side effects. (a) The Node harness does `await import(pathToFileURL(file))`, which runs all top-level code: a `main()`, `app.listen(3000)` (EADDRINUSE against their own dev server, then a 5 s hang) or CLI argv parsing all fire on each save. The 'JS/TS module safety' rule exists only in mech 12, not mech 11. (b) cwd is the workspace folder, so a todo app's `save_todos()` called by a spec overwrites the learner's real todos.json on every save. (c) `--permission --allow-fs-read=<tmpdir>` as written cannot even read harness.mjs (in extensionUri), the learner's file or node_modules. It also does NOT block network: I checked on Node 24.11.1 here, and fetch() under --permission returned 200. (d) Python 'Same limits' has no write or network restriction at all.
issues.fix: Run learner code with cwd = a fresh temp dir, never the workspace. Put the workspace on sys.path or NODE resolution, read-only. Node: `--permission --allow-fs-read=<workspace>,<harness dir>,<tmp> --allow-fs-write=<tmp>`. Apply mech 12's top-level-safety check in mech 11 too, and when it fails, report the teachable nudge 'wrap entry code in `if (require.main === module)` / `import.meta.main`' instead of importing. Python: install a PEP 578 audit hook (sys.addaudithook) in harness.py that raises on open() in write mode outside tmp, and on subprocess.Popen, socket.connect, os.remove/rename and shutil.*. Document network as unblocked for Node and rely on staticDeny only for model-written code.

issues.issue: sameOutput as specified grades wrong exactly where misconceptions live. JSON.parse('2.0') === JSON.parse('2') is true (I checked), so a learner who answers '2' for Python `print(4/2)` is graded correct, which breaks every numbers-int-float and integer-division probe. The naive ' -> " and None->null rewrites corrupt real output: Python prints `["it's", 'None']` (I checked), which becomes unparseable or wrong. Node prints `{ a: 1, b: 'x' }` and `[ 'a', 'b' ]` (unquoted keys, padded), which is not JSON, so it falls back to exact string compare and marks `{a: 1}` wrong on whitespace. Arrays over about 72 characters print across several lines, which breaks the 'exactly one line' rule. A typed `'hi'` vs printed `hi` is also unhandled.
issues.fix: Use a language-aware canonicaliser, not regex+JSON. Python: tokenize both sides with a small literal parser that keeps int vs float vs str types (or run ast.literal_eval in the already-detected runtime, about 100 ms) and compare (type, value). JS: require probes to print through a bundled `show(x)` prelude that emits JSON.stringify with sorted keys, and parse learner answers with a JSON5-style parser. Treat a quoted answer to an unquoted printed str as a distinct 'repr-vs-str' outcome rather than plain wrong. Add test cases: 2 vs 2.0, apostrophes, 'None' inside strings, Node inspect spacing, and multi-line arrays.

issues.issue: The background budget cannot support the prefetch the speed claims rely on. The startup burst is plan + gate + spec ladder (+repair) + 2-6 atom-pack calls (+40% repair), which is about 7-10 calls in about 5 min. Per 5-15 min task: gate N+1, spec N+1 (+repair), 1-2 packs, polish review, hint ladder, up to 2 escalation lessons, follow-up and optional MisconceptionGuess per unmatched wrong answer, about 5-9 calls. At the targeted 3-5 tasks/hour that is 15-45 calls/hour against a default of 20/hour. The success metrics ('<=8 per task' and '<=20/hour' with 3-5 tasks/hour) contradict each other. When the window is full, priority 0-1 jobs 'wait' with no bound, so the next task's gate and specs are missing and it silently falls back to the slow Check-my-work path. Hint prefetch (priority 2, the basis of '0 s hints') is the first thing dropped. Background jobs also inherit codexFast=true (priority tier, more plan usage) even though nobody waits on them.
issues.fix: Merge TaskGate + SpecLadder into one TaskPrep call per task. Run background jobs with fast=false, keeping fast only for foreground calls. Reserve budget: e.g. 4/hour kept for hint ladders, and MisconceptionGuess at priority 3 capped at 2 per task. Give priority-1 jobs a deadline (e.g. needed-by = predicted task end) and specify the degraded path when it is missed. Make the default budget tier-aware (start at 20, halve on the first 'plan limit' error, log per-hour usage in the tooltip). Fix the success metrics so they agree with the target tasks/hour.

issues.issue: The Python flags and env are inconsistent. `-I` implies -E, so the PYTHONIOENCODING and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE env vars in the spec do nothing. I checked locally: under -I with PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1, sys.flags.dont_write_bytecode is 0. As a result, harness imports of sibling modules write __pycache__ into the learner's workspace on every save. `-I` (and its implied -s) plus a minimal env without APPDATA also hides user site-packages, where pip installs by default on Windows for non-admin installs ('Defaulting to user installation'). Specs then fail with ImportError while the same code runs fine in their terminal.
issues.fix: Model snippets: `-I -B -X utf8`. Learner code (specs and own-code probes): `-E -B -X utf8` without -I/-s, keep APPDATA/LOCALAPPDATA/USERPROFILE in env, and add the workspace and the file's dir to sys.path explicitly. Add a runner test asserting no __pycache__ appears in a fixture workspace.

issues.issue: Interpreter detection will usually pick the wrong Python. `python.defaultInterpreterPath` is only a default and is not the interpreter selected in the Python extension (that is kept in the extension's own storage). 'The interpreter from the last successful terminal command' gives a first token like `python`, which resolves through the terminal's activated venv PATH, not the extension host's PATH. So venv packages are missing in spec runs. Also, on this machine `python` is the WindowsApps alias: I measured 205 ms per run through the alias vs 96 ms for the real exe, which doubles every run's cost.
issues.fix: Order: (1) the ms-python.python extension API (`@vscode/python-extension` -> environments.getActiveEnvironmentPath(workspaceFolder)) when installed; (2) workspace .venv/venv/env Scripts/python.exe or bin/python; (3) PATH candidates. After the hello-world succeeds, print sys.executable and cache that absolute path, spawning it directly from then on. Re-detect on activation (cheap) instead of trusting a persisted Project.runtime.

issues.issue: The TypeScript runtime plan doesn't work for real projects. `process.features.typescript` must come from the spawned system node: the extension host's own Node (Electron, Node 20 in VS Code 1.93) has no type stripping, and the spec doesn't say which process is checked. Node type stripping rejects extensionless or `.js` relative imports of .ts files (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND) and non-erasable syntax (enum, namespace, parameter properties). Normal learner TS projects written for tsc or bundlers will crash the harness. The fallback `npx --no-install tsx` fails whenever tsx isn't installed in the project or globally; it isn't on PATH on this machine.
issues.fix: Detect with `node -p process.features.typescript` (a spawned process). In harness.mjs, register a module.register() resolve hook that maps extensionless and .js specifiers to an existing .ts file. Check <workspace>/node_modules/.bin/tsx before npx. Tell the AtomPack and SpecLadder prompts to use erasable TS syntax only. If none of this works, set TS spec ladders to applicable=false with a one-line reason, instead of crashing every save.

issues.issue: Node permission flags vary by version. `--permission` is the stable name only from Node 22.13 / 23.5. Node 20.x and 22.0-22.12 need `--experimental-permission` and exit with 'bad option' on `--permission`. detectRuntime's hello-world runs without the flag, so detection passes and then every real snippet fails. Note also that this machine has two Nodes on PATH (24.11.1 and 23.9.0).
issues.fix: Run the detection hello-world with the exact argv later used for snippets, including the permission flag. Pick the flag by parsed version (stable >= 22.13 or >= 23.5, experimental for 20.0-22.12). Below 20, run without the permission model and rely on staticDeny plus the temp cwd. Cache the absolute node path you resolved.

issues.issue: JS/TS completion items cannot fail correctly. staticDeny bans `require(`, `import` and `process.`, so the 'assert lines' harness cannot use node:assert or set an exit code, and console.assert only prints and exits 0. Result: any syntactically valid fill passes, verification drops every wrongFill because it 'passes', and completion grading for JS/TS checks nothing.
issues.fix: The runner prepends a bundled prelude defining `function check(cond, msg) { if (!cond) throw new Error('CHECK ' + msg) }`, so an uncaught throw gives a non-zero exit. The AtomPack prompt must use check(...) in JS/TS harnesses, and verification rejects a JS harness without check(. Do the same for failingHarnessLine parsing: match the 'CHECK' marker rather than relying on stack line arithmetic.

issues.issue: Using a real file in globalStorage as the Atom Pad causes several problems. Pylance, Ruff and ESLint analyse it: `___` placeholders give 'not defined' errors and half-typed answers give syntax errors, all shown in the Problems panel and status-bar error count. Closing a dirty file prompts to save, so exit needs a focus-juggling `workbench.action.files.revert`. Hot exit restores a stale dirty pad tab after a reload. `preview: true` means a single click in the Explorer replaces the pad tab when the pad's group is active, which onDidChangeTabs then treats as Esc and aborts the atom. With files.autoSave on, it is saved constantly. The file must also exist on disk before openTextDocument, which the spec doesn't mention.
issues.fix: Register an in-memory FileSystemProvider for scheme `deliberate-pad` (vscode.workspace.registerFileSystemProvider, present in 1.93). Language servers mostly ignore unknown schemes, and Monitor.isCode already excludes them. Open with preview: false. Before tabGroups.close, call document.save(), which writes to memory, so there is no prompt and no revert. On activation, close any leftover deliberate-pad tabs. Pad and skeleton then need no path-prefix exclusions.

issues.issue: AI autocomplete contaminates evidence. GitHub Copilot or another inline-completion extension will suggest the answer after `# -> ` and fill `___` blanks in the pad, and will write project code. Paste detection only matches the clipboard, so assisted inserts count as the learner's own correct, fast answers and as unaided task solves (recordSolve 'task' evidence). That breaks the claim that 'the learner produces the code' and the guess rate of 0.03.
issues.fix: In Monitor, flag any single contentChange that inserts 12 or more non-whitespace characters, has reason undefined, does not match the clipboard, and is not a snippet the pad inserted itself. In the pad, mark that item's evidence assisted (discard it). In project files, add it to task.assistedChars, alongside pastedChars, in recordSolve. At first pad open, if vscode.extensions.getExtension('GitHub.copilot') is active, show a one-time note and offer a per-language toggle.

issues.issue: The Testing API causes side effects on every save. In the installed VS Code build, `testing.openTesting` defaults to 'openOnTestStart'; I found it in workbench.desktop.main.js. That opens Test Results on every save-triggered run, replacing the terminal the learner is using. In a red-green ladder, specs 2-5 are always red while spec 1 is being built, so each save reports several failures with TestMessage.location on the learner's def line; depending on `testing.automaticallyOpenPeekView` (check its 1.93 default), a peek can cover their code. Registering the profile with supportsContinuousRun=true and also running on save gives duplicate runs when continuous mode is on.
issues.fix: Only the current target spec (the first red) is reported failed; later ones are reported skipped, with no message location. Save-triggered runs go to your own decorations and the tempo bar, and are published to the TestController only for runs the learner started or when request.continuous is on (then don't also run on save). Spike the openTesting and peek behaviour on 1.93 before committing to the Testing view as the primary surface.

issues.issue: The harness rules for loading learner modules break normal beginner code. The Python 'AST-strip loader' drops assignments with calls, so `PATTERN = re.compile(...)`, `counts = Counter()` and `DATA = load_defaults()` vanish and specs fail with NameError, and it contradicts the separate claim that 'input() at import raises EOFError -> teachable failure', since stripped code never runs. In JS, calls are evaluated over the module's exports, but beginners rarely export functions from a script, so every spec fails with ReferenceError and no useful nudge.
issues.fix: Python: import the module normally under a non-'__main__' name, with the audit hook and builtins.input patched to raise a tagged exception. When that exception or argv access happens at import, report 'top-level code runs on import: move it under if __name__ == "__main__"' as the spec nudge. JS: compare exported names with the interface; for 'defined but not exported', show a specific nudge, and have the task card's interface line say 'export'.

issues.issue: Spec ladder verification in an isolated temp dir will fail for most later tasks. Tasks are designed to 'build on the code from the previous one' and the prompt says 'reuse an existing file if the task extends it'. The reference then needs the learner's sibling modules or existing helper functions, which are absent in globalStorageUri/tmp/<uuid>, so ModuleNotFoundError or NameError drops the specs and gives applicable=false.
