Separately, staticDeny (no os/pathlib/open/sys) would reject any reference that touches files.
issues.fix: Verify against a temp copy of the workspace's source files (respecting a size cap and ignore globs), with the interface file's target functions replaced by the reference. Build the stub from the learner's current file with only the interface functions swapped for raising stubs. Run the reference under the learner-code sandbox (cwd = temp, audit hook) instead of staticDeny.

issues.issue: Spec `call` and `expected` strings are model output that the harness evaluates (eval in the module namespace or new Function), but the strict callExpr validator is applied only to own-code probes (mech 12). The SpecLadder prompt includes workspace file content, so a comment in a cloned repo can inject an arbitrary expression that then runs with the learner's privileges on every save.
issues.fix: Run the mech-12 validator (AST: one Call whose func is a Name in interface.functions and whose args are literals only) on every spec call and hidden call before storing it; drop failures. Parse `expected` only with ast.literal_eval or JSON.parse, never eval. Give `deliberate.localExecution`, `deliberate.codexPath` and any interpreter override `"scope": "machine"` in package.json, so a workspace .vscode/settings.json cannot point them at a repo script or switch execution to 'all'.

issues.issue: The content rules make project-specific concepts impossible to atomise. Probes are 8-line stdout-only snippets, imports are limited to math/collections/itertools/functools, and staticDeny bans open/sys/os/import/require/process. That rules out argparse, JSON files, requests, Flask/Express routes, React state, DOM, SQL and pandas, and even canonical tags in the spec's own list (file-read-lines, modules-imports). Acceptance needs at least 2 surviving probes, so these packs fail, and no fallback is defined. The gate then routes 'missed pattern' to an atom that can never exist, and Teach loops through foreground generation.
issues.fix: Add a per-tag import allowlist (json, re, datetime with fixed values, argparse with an explicit argv list, io.StringIO standing in for files, dataclasses). Allow third-party imports that the detected runtime can actually import, checked by find_spec, still under the sandbox. Add ConceptState.probeable=false after one failed pack, with a defined fallback for such concepts: which-pattern and contrast items keyed by the model (verified=false, low weight) plus the escalation lesson. Never retry the pack in the foreground.

issues.issue: The latency estimates for verification and foreground Teach are too optimistic. One atom's verification is about 26 process runs (4 probes x2, about 12 mutants, example, fill, empty-blank, about 2 wrongFills, 2 contrast). Measured here: about 96 ms per Python run with the real exe and 205 ms through the alias, about 80 ms for Node and about 130 ms for Node .ts. That is 2.5-5.5 s per atom run one after another, not '1-2 s per pack'. 'Teach on cache miss: about 10-15 s' ignores codex exec start-up, a large structured output (pattern + 4 probes x 3 mutants + example + completion + contrast) and the 40% repair round trip. A realistic figure is 25-45 s.
issues.fix: Build a batch runner: one interpreter process takes a JSON list of snippets and executes each in a fresh namespace with stdout captured and a per-snippet watchdog (Python: exec with redirect_stdout plus a faulthandler/thread timeout; Node: the vm module plus a worker with a timeout). That brings a pack down to one spawn. For a foreground cache miss, generate a 'probe-only mini atom' (2 probes from 2 groups plus 1 completion) at low effort, and prefetch the rest in the background. Re-measure against the stated targets.

issues.issue: The plan call is the single gate for everything, and its failure paths are missing. The prompt now asks for up to 6x6 = 36 tasks plus 8-25 tagged concepts at high effort; the output is large and 100 s is optimistic. If it fails, times out (300 s) or hits a plan limit, the learner is left with a shell project with no tasks and no retry. A window reload drops the in-flight job, and nothing on activation re-enqueues it ('the next trigger' doesn't exist for the plan). The plan's `language` field can also disagree with the language detected at t=0.
issues.fix: Split into PlanOutline (milestones plus concepts with tags, medium effort) and TaskBatch (tasks for milestone 1 now, milestone k+1 when milestone k starts). On failure, push a card with Retry and keep placement results. On activation, reconcile: if project.placement.planPending and there are no milestones, enqueue 'plan'. Pass the detected language as fixed input and drop it from PlanSchema.

issues.issue: Removing the busy lock leaves no replacement guard for local flows. The pad, gate QuickPick, sprint, what-if InputBoxes, own-predict InputBox and pre-hint step are long-running async flows that can overlap: a sprint auto-opens during a foreground wait while the gate is up; Ctrl+Alt+H or Alt+N fires during an atom; startTask from the Roadmap tab while the pad is open makes pad exit restore resumePhase on the wrong task; hint() can run twice at once from tempo click + keybinding + auto mode. The race rule (check createdAt/taskId) covers only open-ended grades, but plan, gate, spec and pack results also write project state after 'Start a New Goal'.
issues.fix: Add an InteractionLock (one modal flow at a time). Other flows go to the Scheduler queue instead of opening. startTask, newProject and resetProfile first abort the active flow (counted as Esc) and cancelWhere(taskId). Every background apply() checks a generation token (project.createdAt + taskId + a task-switch counter) before writing anything. Keep per-task single-flight on hint().

issues.issue: The hint prefetch key will almost never match. codeHash = sha1(codeSnapshot() minus the timestamp line), but gatherCodeContext (src/context.ts) also embeds `<<CURSOR>>` at the cursor line, 'N min ago' for terminal runs, and 'code was edited AFTER this run' notes. The hash changes whenever the cursor moves or a minute passes, so 'hint:<taskId>:<codeHash>' lookups miss, every serve becomes an on-demand call, and the '>=70% served from prefetch' target can't be reached. The '<=2 unused prefetches' cap also burns out quickly.
issues.fix: Key the prefetch by taskId only, with validity decided by the staleness rules (anchor lineText still present, fewer than 20 changed lines, same error set). For the hash, use content-only hashes of the task files plus the normalised error set, computed separately from the prompt rendering.

issues.issue: Killing the Codex process is incomplete. On POSIX, child.kill('SIGKILL') kills only the direct child. With an npm-installed codex, that is the Node shim, and the native codex binary keeps running and keeps using the plan. In the current codex.ts the timeout path on win32 (shell: true for .cmd shims) also kills only cmd.exe. Cancelled speculative jobs would therefore still cost plan usage.
issues.fix: In proc.spawnCapped: on POSIX, spawn with detached: true and kill the group with process.kill(-child.pid, 'SIGKILL'); on win32, use taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F for both abort and timeout. Add a test that spawns a parent which starts a sleeping grandchild, then asserts the grandchild is gone after abort.

issues.issue: State persistence won't scale and isn't safe across windows. Store.flush() writes the whole Learner to globalState on each save() (debounced 300 ms, called on every graded item and every 30 s tick). With evidenceLog capped at 2000 plus 30 Evidence per concept x 50 concepts at about 300 B each, that is over 1 MB per write, and globalState changes are sent to every open VS Code window. Two windows on two projects each hold a full Learner copy, so the last write wins and erases the other window's evidence and mastery. The AtomCache JSON written from two windows has the same problem.
issues.fix: Keep only compact ConceptState summaries in globalState. Append Evidence to globalStorageUri/evidence-YYYY-MM.jsonl, keep per-concept rolling stats in memory, and rebuild them from the log on load. Before writing, re-read globalState and merge per concept by lastAt/evidence ids, or take a lock file in globalStorage. Do the same for the atom cache (merge by item id).

issues.issue: One item can mark a concept mastered or unknown. A single correct predict takes P from .30 to .928 (g .03), which with tested=true and no fragility is isMastered, after which the concept 'costs 0 in gates and is never re-taught'. That rests on one recognition item, and the guess rate of .03 is wrong for probes with tiny answer spaces (True/False, 0/1, 'error'), which mutants often produce. In the other direction, one '?' (or an accidental Enter on an empty answer, which the spec treats as don't-know) takes P to .009, and propagation caps every descendant up to 3 hops at <= .26. One skip on a root such as variables-assignment during placement collapses the DAG and floods atoms. The test expectations (.928 exactly) also ignore the T = .05 'feedback shown' transition that the same spec applies.
issues.fix: Derive the guess rate per item from its answer space (bool .5, small int .1-.2, structured .03, bare 'error' .3). For isMastered, require correct answers from at least 2 sibling groups, including at least 1 produce item (completion, spec or own-predict). An empty submit re-prompts; only an explicit '?' counts as don't-know, at weight .5. Downward propagation needs 2 wrong items, or applies only 1 hop from a single one. Fix the test numbers to include the learning transition.

issues.issue: autoSave breaks both the spec trigger and the pause detector. With files.autoSave = afterDelay (common), every short typing pause saves. Specs run on half-typed code (harness 'errored' spam and flickering red/error gutter icons). Every auto-save with 0 errors also counts as a 'clean save' natural pause, so the Scheduler's pop rule (pause in the last 20 s) is almost always satisfied, which defeats the anti-interruption design.
issues.fix: Use onWillSaveTextDocument's reason (TextDocumentSaveReason.AfterDelay/FocusOut exists in 1.93). Only manual saves count as pauses. For auto-saves, run specs after 1.5 s idle and only when the file has no syntax-level error diagnostics.

issues.issue: The spec says V1 'must work for any language' but ships Python/JS/TS only, and other languages lose verified keys, mutants, completion, specs and own-code probes. Yet Go 1.26, Java 25 and rustc 1.97 are installed on this machine. Predict items don't need execution at grade time, only at verification time (the recorded output is the key), so compiled-language latency isn't a blocker for the core loop. Measured: `go run` 22 s cold, 0.4-0.8 s warm.
issues.fix: Add a RuntimeAdapter table {detect, wrapSnippet, run} for go (`go run`), java (single-file `java File.java`) and rust (rustc to a temp exe, then run). Use it for background verification (batch all of a pack's snippets into one program with a case switch, so there is one compile per pack) and for completion grading with a visible 'running...' (1-2 s is acceptable there). Warm the Go build cache in the background at detection. Keep neutral pseudocode items only for runtimes that really aren't available.

issues.issue: Own-code predict items leak answers. 'Probe inputs, first choice: calls from the task's spec ladder, visible and hidden.' Visible spec titles ('1 empty argv -> {}') and TestMessage.diff show the expected value, so the learner can copy it without understanding their code. Using hidden-spec calls reveals the inputs that exist to catch hard-coded answers.
issues.fix: Never use spec inputs for own-predict. Use inputs from OwnCodeProbeSchema or locally mutated spec inputs (change one literal: empty, boundary, duplicate), with the result checked to differ from every visible spec's input.

issues.issue: Sprint wait-filling conflicts with 'the learner may keep coding'. For Check my work (30-40 s), fgWithSprint auto-opens the pad with focus when the window is focused, so the learner is pulled out of their code. The spec also has the sprint used *inside* an open atom (escalation lesson miss, 'pack job in flight: wait up to 30 s with a sprint'), which would need nested pad state save and restore that isn't specified.
issues.fix: Auto-open only if there has been no edit in the last 8 s. Otherwise, enqueue a 'sprint' action. Never nest: when the pad is busy, show '# preparing lesson... (~10 s)' in the pad header and run the background call.

issues.issue: Keybinding scoping is incomplete. Only escape has a when-clause. ctrl+enter / ctrl+shift+enter would override the defaults editor.action.insertLineAfter/Before everywhere unless scoped. The escape clause misses editorHoverVisible, notificationToastsVisible, renameInputVisible and inlineChatVisible, so pressing Esc to close a hover or toast aborts the atom. Alt+N won't reach the extension while focus is in the integrated terminal (not in terminal.integrated.commandsToSkipShell), and on macOS alt+n is a dead key.
issues.fix: Scope atomSubmit and atomSubmitGuess to `deliberate.atomFocused && editorTextFocus && !suggestWidgetVisible`. Add the missing negations to escape, or make abort a double-Esc within 600 ms. Add mac keybindings (ctrl+alt+n). Document that Alt+N does not work from the terminal, or provide a status-bar click as the primary trigger.

issues.issue: Seed banks are verified on the developer's runtime (Python 3.14, Node 24) at package time. A learner's older Python (missing str.removeprefix, match, newer error names) or different Node (util.inspect formatting has changed between versions) can produce different outputs, so the bundled keys are wrong for them, and placement grades are wrong at the moment trust matters most.
issues.fix: After detectRuntime, re-verify the language's seed bank in the background with the batch runner (about 1 spawn). Overwrite recorded outputs and drop items that now fail, before placement serves them. Placement can start on items already re-verified.

issues.issue: With the vscode-lm provider, background jobs would call sendRequest outside a user action. The typings say the first call shows a consent dialog and 'must only be called in response to a user action', so a modal can appear in the middle of coding. Usage-limit detection only recognises the 'Codex plan limit reached' prefix; the Anthropic RateLimitError and LanguageModelError.Blocked messages are not handled.
issues.fix: At Start (a user action), make one tiny request to obtain consent. Background jobs check context.languageModelAccessInformation.canSendRequest(model) and skip when it isn't true. Give LlmError a `kind: 'limit'|'auth'|'format'|'other'` set by every provider, and have the JobQueue pause on kind=limit.

issues.issue: Mutant attribution is ambiguous. Verification only checks that a mutant's output differs from the original. Two mutants for different beliefs often produce the same output (common with off-by-one beliefs), and a mutant can equal a likely typo. A match then names a belief arbitrarily, and the 6x odds multiplier pushes it towards ACTIVE.
issues.fix: During verification, merge or drop mutants with identical outputs (an ambiguous output records wrong evidence but no misconceptionId). Require the mutant diff to be a single line. Treat an answer within edit distance 1 of the actual output as a probable slip, with no misconception update.

issues.issue: Seed and plan concept ids diverge. Placement records evidence on seed ids before the plan exists. The plan may return a different id for the same tag, several concepts with one tag, or tag 'other'. 'Map by tag' has no stored alias, so evidence is orphaned or duplicated, and snapshot() shows both.
issues.fix: Add a tag index and ConceptState.aliases. When the plan lands, merge a plan concept with the seed concept of the same tag (keep the seed id as canonical and record the plan id as an alias). For many-to-one, make the seed concept a prerequisite of each plan concept. slug() lookups go through the alias map.

issues.issue: Spec ladder timing and heavy imports are unspecified or too optimistic. SpecLadder (medium, about 30-40 s, plus verification and repair) usually lands after the gate (low, about 10 s), so building starts without specs, and the spec doesn't say whether specs attach mid-task. A learner module importing pandas, matplotlib or flask costs 1-3 s+ per spawn on Windows, so 'spec verdict < 1 s' fails and the 5 s timeout can trip.
issues.fix: Attach specs when they land if the task is still building and nothing is green, using a tempo action 'specs ready (5)'. Measure import time on the first run; above 1 s, switch to a persistent per-task worker that reloads only changed workspace modules (importlib.reload / a fresh vm context), or show a 'running specs...' state.

issues.issue: Editor clutter has no single owner. The learner's def line can carry hint rung after-text, a failure-signature nudge, own-predict feedback and what-if line-through at once, from separate decoration types with no precedence; after-text on long lines renders off-screen. The 'Predict ...' CodeLens appearing and disappearing shifts code down a line during work. A task ending chains up to six quick inputs (2 what-if InputBoxes, gate pick, feedback pick, plan pick, feedback pick), and the what-if InputBoxes use the default ignoreFocusOut = false, so clicking into the editor hides them and counts as a skip.
issues.fix: Add one LineAnnotationManager: at most one after-text per line, chosen by priority (hint > spec nudge > own-predict), with the rest folded into the hover. Show own-predict offers in the tempo bar or as the hover's command link instead of a CodeLens, or keep a lens permanently so lines don't jump. Put feedback into the next QuickPick's title instead of separate pickers, set ignoreFocusOut: true on what-ifs, and offer 'later' as a button.

issues.issue: Fluency is measured against the learner's own speed. par = parSec x speedFactor, where speedFactor is the learner's own running median ratio, so by construction about half of their answers are at or under par. 'Fluent' then reflects consistency, not the absolute speed the user asked for.
issues.fix: Use the unscaled parSec for the Fluent chip and the Pace metrics. Use speedFactor only to decide Fragile (slow relative to self) and to discard latency outliers.

issues.issue: insertSnippet in 1.93 has no keepWhitespace option; the typings show only undoStopBefore and undoStopAfter. Snippet text is re-indented to the insertion line, and tabs are converted using editor settings, which can corrupt the indentation of Python completion items inserted anywhere other than column 0 of an empty document. The spec also lists `TerminalShellExecution.commandLine, exitCode`, but exitCode is on TerminalShellExecutionEndEvent, not the execution.
issues.fix: Always clear the pad and insert the snippet at (0,0) of an empty document, built with 4-space indentation, and test it with tabs and 2-space user settings. Read exitCode from the end event, as monitor.ts already does.

issues.issue: Smaller gaps in the existing code and tests. viewModel still marks 'mastered' with MASTERY_TARGET 0.8, while isMastered requires P >= .85 and more, so the Progress tab and the gate-skip logic disagree. test/vscode-stub.ts has none of createQuickPick, createInputBox, tabGroups, tests or decorations, but flow.test is supposed to drive the gate, pad and spec paths. Project.runtime is described as 'cached for the session' but is stored in workspaceState, which persists across sessions. scripts/verify-seeds.mjs cannot import src/runner.ts without tsx.
issues.fix: Have viewModel use isMastered and chip(). Inject GateUi, AtomRunner, SpecRunner and InputFlow interfaces into Coach, and give flow.test fakes for them, so the vscode stub stays small. Keep runtime in memory only, re-detecting on activation. Run the seed verifier with `tsx scripts/verify-seeds.ts`.

proposals.thesis: Replace the 'micro-lesson card + free-text check' with a probe-first CONCEPT ATOM: a 60-120 second loop that runs in a scratch editor beside the project file and is graded locally. Nothing in it waits on a model. Every atom opens with a test, not text. Pretesting and rapid-assessment research supports this: Kalyuga and Sweller's first-step tests correlated up to .92 with full solutions and took 3-5x less time. A learner who already knows the idea (right, sure and fast) leaves in about 15 seconds; the expertise-reversal effect says worked examples hurt people who don't need them. Only a failed probe opens the faded sequence: a subgoal-labelled worked example, then a completion or Parsons problem on a new surface (Ericson et al. 2017: Parsons problems took much less time than writing the code, with the same learning and retention), then a contrasting-case discrimination. Patterns are first-class, matching the learner's belief. Each atom teaches one template, in the sense of Soloway's programming plans and Xie et al.'s trace, then read-template, then write-template skill ladder, and the learner builds a Pattern Deck. All atom content is generated in batches while the learner codes. It is then verified by running it locally with the learner's installed runtime. That includes 'misconception mutants': copies of the code edited to behave the way a named wrong belief predicts. If a wrong prediction exactly matches a mutant's real output, the extension names the gap in milliseconds. Every answer carries a free confidence bit (Ctrl+Enter = sure, Ctrl+Shift+Enter = guessing) and a latency. These feed a Bayesian (BKT) learner model with four states: misconception (confident-wrong, which gets hypercorrection), not-learned, fragile (unsure-right or slow) and fluent. Model calls move off the critical path. Placement runs while the roadmap is being generated. Retrieval sprints fill the 100-second review waits. Open-ended grading runs in the background. The model is kept for the work only it can do: judging the learner's own code, giving hints on it, and generating content ahead of time. Today one concept gap costs about 5-7 minutes, 1-2 of them spent waiting. The new design costs 15-110 seconds with no waiting.
mechanisms: A1 Probe-first Concept Atom in an in-editor Atom Pad (the 60-120s loop)
A2 Self-verifying Atom Packs: batched prefetch, local execution, misconception mutants
A3 Confidence x correctness x latency evidence model (BKT with misconception / fragile / fluent states)
A4 Placement that runs during roadmap generation: adaptive, prerequisite-graph inference, locally graded
A5 Task gate: pattern pick + plan Parsons instead of a free-text approach essay
A6 Never-idle: wait-filling interleaved retrieval sprints + non-blocking open-ended grading
A7 Predict-before-run on the learner's own project code

proposals.thesis:
Make diagnosis do the teaching. Today a concept block works like this: the LLM writes about 250 words, the learner reads them, types a free-text answer and waits about 10s for an LLM grade. That is about 4-5 minutes for one noisy piece of evidence. Replace it with a stream of micro-probes, each answered with one keystroke and graded locally:
- multiple-choice questions where every wrong option is tagged with a named misconception
- two-tier items (answer plus reason)
- predict-the-output
- Parsons problems
- spot-the-bug

Each answer records the chosen option, the learner's confidence and the response time. It feeds a Bayesian learner model over the plan's prerequisite graph: knowledge tracing per concept, plus a probability for each named misconception. The model picks the next item that gives the most information per second. It infers known prerequisites instead of asking about them. It teaches only when it sees a specific wrong belief: a refutation of 40 words or fewer with a contrast pair whose outputs were checked by running them, then a re-probe with a different surface that proves the fix.

The deepest probes use the learner's own code: "predict what your function returns" and "predict what this one-token change to your line would do". They are graded by actually running the code, never by a model.

Model calls leave the critical path. They only:
- write item banks in background batches, checked by local execution before use
- pre-write escalation lessons in case they are needed
- judge genuinely open-ended work (approach plans, code review, hints)

Expected effect:
- Placement drops from about 10 minutes to about 2, and runs while the roadmap is still being generated.
- A concept block drops from about 4-5 minutes for 1 observation to 30-90 seconds for 3-6 observations.
- Skipping material the learner already knows costs about 10 seconds.
mechanisms: B1 Verified misconception bank: written in the background, checked by local execution
B2 Probe Deck: keyboard-only rapid probes with one-keystroke confidence and response timing
B3 Learner model v2: Bayesian knowledge tracing plus misconception probabilities over the prerequisite graph, with information-per-second item selection
B4 Short, contingent concept block: probe, then a 40-word refutation with a run-checked contrast pair, then a re-probe; full lesson only on escalation
B5 Own-code probes: predict-your-function and what-if mutants, graded by running the learner's code
B6 Passive evidence from the build loop: error signatures weighted by fix time, typing gaps by which hint helped, paste detection

proposals.thesis: Rebuild the concept block as reps done in the editor instead of 'read a 250-word card in the sidebar, type an answer, wait for the model'. A rep is a 10 to 120 second run of small actions that are graded locally: predict, spot, order, fill, run. Reps come from Concept Packs, which the model batch-generates in the background before they are needed. A pack holds a pattern card of 60 words or fewer (name, when to use it, a code shape with holes, the pitfall), 8 probes across four depths (recall, trace, apply, transfer), a runnable worked example, and a kata with tests. The answer keys come from running the code on the learner's machine, not from the model. Probe first, teach only on a miss: a strip of one-keystroke Quick Pick probes decides in about 30 seconds whether a concept needs teaching at all. The depth of the miss picks the remedy: the pattern card, a trace stepper, or a 2-minute lab file. Tasks arrive as coach-authored failing tests that turn green on save, so 'done' and 'stuck on what' are known locally and per concept. The hint ladder is prefetched while the stuck meter rises and appears instantly as a comment thread on the line it concerns. The model is kept for genuinely open-ended judgment (plan quality, explain-back, design review). Those calls run asynchronously: the learner keeps moving and the verdict lands on the relevant line. Every keystroke produces typed evidence: which distractor was picked and which misconception it maps to, answer latency, confidence, and which test stayed red and for how long. That evidence feeds a local mastery model that accounts for guessing and slips. Gaps are found at the level of a single misconception or line, while the learner spends almost no time waiting or reading. The sidebar becomes a history and progress dashboard. The editor, the status bar and the Testing view are where learning happens.
mechanisms: C1 Probe Strip: one-keystroke Quick Pick probes from prefetched, run-verified Concept Packs
C2 Spec-as-Tests: each task arrives as 3-6 coach-authored failing tests in the Testing view that turn green as the learner codes
C3 Lab Rep: a 2-minute runnable concept file (predict, break it, kata) that replaces the 250-word lesson card
C4 Trace Stepper: step through a worked example (or the learner's own selection) in the editor, predicting values at stop points
C5 Anchored coach threads: plan, hints, review and explain-back live on the learner's own lines (Comments API), are graded asynchronously, and hints are prefetched
C6 Tempo bar and pause scheduler: one status-bar 'next action', and nudges only at natural pauses, so the sidebar is optional

proposals.thesis: Make the pattern, not the concept, the unit of teaching, and make every concept block a short burst of reps the learner answers at keyboard speed instead of a lesson to read. Each concept the roadmap needs is broken into 3-6 named patterns, each with a shape of at most 3 lines (for example "Tally with dict.get": counts[k] = counts.get(k, 0) + 1). Each pattern ships with a bank of objective items generated in the background and checked locally: recognise, predict output, produce with a hole, produce from blank, spot the bug, and a near-miss transfer item. The answer key for predict items is the snippet's real output from running it locally, and produce items are checked by running tests locally. The concept block becomes a 45-150 second burst in a panel beside the code, and production happens in a real editor buffer. It ends as soon as the learner has proven they can apply the pattern (a blank produce plus a transfer item, both right and under the time target). Recording accuracy and latency on every rep gives a faster and finer gap signal than free-text answers. The distractor the learner picks names the misconception. A pattern prerequisite graph traces a failure to its root. A 2x2 of fast/slow by right/wrong tells a gap apart from a misconception and from knowledge that is there but slow. Automaticity is tracked and spaced per pattern. Model calls are kept for open-ended judgment: the roadmap, generating item banks, plan packs, higher hint rungs, Check my work and explain-back. They run ahead of the learner in a concurrent background lane, so they are almost never on the critical path. The project stays the place where patterns get combined. Patterns are drilled alone in seconds, then must show up unprompted in the learner's own code, and that is the final proof of automaticity.
mechanisms: D1 Pattern Atlas: concepts decomposed into drillable patterns with prebuilt, locally-verified item banks
D2 90-second Pattern Burst in a Rep Deck beside the code (replaces the micro-lesson card + free-text check)
D3 Automaticity tracker: latency x accuracy per pattern, fluency gates, per-pattern spacing, sprints and warm-ups
D4 3-minute adaptive placement sweep over the pattern graph, run while the roadmap is generated
D5 Plan-by-patterns gate: pick the patterns, order the steps (replaces the free-text approach essay)
D6 Pattern-aware building: live pattern sightings in the learner's code, instant pattern-level hint rungs, prefetched model hints
D7 Zero-wait orchestration: background job lanes, prefetch schedule, async grading, reps while waiting

proposals.thesis: The learner's hands give the answers, the computer grades them, and the model writes content ahead of time in the background. Each concept block starts with a probe. The learner first gets a 5-15 second item (predict the output, find the buggy line, or fill one blank). Its answer key was verified by running it locally before it was ever shown, so grading takes 0 ms. If the answer is right and under par time, there is no teaching. If it is wrong, the learner sees only the 30-word fix written for the exact wrong option they picked, then a fresh version of the same item. Project work becomes a red-green spec ladder: the coach writes the failing specs (never the solution) and the learner turns them green, with results on every save in under a second. Depth comes from three things: 10-second predictions about the code the learner just wrote, Navigator hints that only ask questions and are attached to the exact line, and bug hunts in a mutated copy of the learner's own code. Every micro-interaction produces evidence: correct or not, time against par, which misconception the chosen option maps to, item level, and whether help was used. A local learner model consumes that evidence, so within seconds a gap is traced to a concept, a specific misconception and its root prerequisite, with no wait on a model. Model calls leave the critical path. They are batched and prefetched (one task ahead, or when the stuck meter reaches 'warm') and verified by local execution. The only remaining synchronous use is open-ended judgment, and even that is graded in the background so the learner never waits.
mechanisms: E1 Red-Green Spec Ladder (tests are the lesson plan)
E2 Probe-first concept blocks in the Arena (the miss is the lesson)
E3 Pause probes: predict your own code (CodeLens answer buttons)
E4 Navigator in the margin: question-only hints anchored to the line, prefetched
E5 Saboteur & Eraser: drills forged from your own code
E6 Tempo engine: levels, par times, streaks (a fast local learner model)
E7 Zero-wait pipeline: background lanes, a verified content bank, a local executor
